title: μSlope: High Compression and Fast Search on Semi-Structured Logs
note: Compression and search engine for semi-structured logs - CPU-only user-space C++ plus a large disk footprint that fits in 257 GB. Concern - full-scale log datasets used in the paper may need to be subsampled

title: Deriving Semantic Checkers from Tests to Detect Silent Failures in Production Distributed Systems
note: T2C is a JVM static/dynamic analysis framework producing runtime checkers; no kernel, no root. Concern: evaluation drives four large JVM distributed systems (HDFS/HBase/Kafka/ZooKeeper) - must be run pseudo-distributed as multiple processes on the one host, and 125 GiB RAM should suffice but overhead numbers may shift.

title: Take Out the TraChe: Maximizing (Tra)nsactional Ca(che) Hit Rate
note: Squarely on-topic: a new cache eviction and prefetching policy (DeToX) driven by transactional dependencies, evaluated with OLTP traces and benchmarks on a single node in user space. Strong fit for a policy-improvement hypothesis with trace-driven replay.

title: From Prefix Cache to Fusion RAG Cache: Accelerating LLM Inference in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
note: RAG inference framework that reuses and selectively recomputes chunk KV caches - KV-cache management for LLM inference - fits one GPU with a small model - concern: no repo located

title: ExChain: Exception Dependency Analysis for Root Cause Diagnosis
note: JVM dynamic taint tracking that links causally related exceptions for root-cause diagnosis of exception-handling failures; single machine, user space, no root. Concerns: needs a Java toolchain via conda and specific versions of the target systems (Hadoop, Solr, Cassandra) to reproduce case studies; taint tracking has high runtime overhead so experiments are CPU-bound but fit in 16 cores.

title: TrainVerify: Equivalence-Based Verification for Distributed LLM Training
note: Although the subject is distributed training, the artifact itself is symbolic/SMT equivalence checking that runs on CPU only - no GPUs and no cluster are needed to reproduce the Llama3-405B and DeepSeek-V3-671B plan verifications. Shape reduction and stage-wise verification are well-defined targets for a "verify faster" hypothesis. Concerns - verifying frontier-scale plans may be memory and time hungry even on 125 GB; success is measured in verification time and coverage, not system throughput.

title: zpoline: a system call hook mechanism based on binary rewriting
note: Explicitly advertises "no kernel change and no additional kernel module" - a pure user-space binary-rewriting mechanism, the best possible match for a no-root machine. Code is a small, well-known, actively maintained C repo. Concerns: the trampoline is instantiated at virtual address 0, which requires vm.mmap_min_addr=0; that sysctl needs root, so the team must check whether the documented --enable-mmap-min-addr-workaround/libzphook path suffices or whether this is a blocker.

title: SimEnc: A High-Performance Similarity-Preserving Encryption Approach for Deduplication of Encrypted Docker Images
note: Deduplication and compression of container image layers - the artifact is a user-space Go program operating on layer tarballs, and dedup ratio plus throughput are directly improvable. Concern: Docker is not installed, so images have to be pulled through the registry HTTP API rather than the Docker CLI

title: GPTuner: A Manual-Reading Database Tuning System via GPT-Guided Bayesian Optimization
note: LLM-guided Bayesian optimization of DBMS knobs. Concern: needs an LLM endpoint or a local 7B model

title: LSMGraph: A High-Performance Dynamic Graph Storage System with Multi-Level CSR
note: LSM-tree + CSR hybrid disk-based graph storage engine; single machine

title: Practical Dynamic Extension for Sampling Indexes
note: Bentley-Saxe dynamization framework for sampling indexes; CPU only, user space

title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
note: Memory-efficient optimizer - drop-in AdamW replacement, 60M-1B LLaMA pre-training runs fit one 24 GB GPU and memory savings are directly measurable - concern: headline 7B numbers need multi-GPU

title: Shrinking VOD Traffic via Renyi-Entropic Optimal Transport
note: Cache-efficiency work: it proposes Renyi entropy as a proxy for the cache footprint of a video catalogue, proves that minimizing it maximizes soft cache hit ratio, and evaluates on a real VOD request trace. Entirely CPU-side optimal-transport computation over a request trace, so the machine is not a constraint. Concern: no official implementation found - I searched the GitHub repository API for the system name and for "optimal transport / soft cache hit ratio" phrasings, checked the ACM DL landing page and the Edinburgh and Surrey institutional repository records, and found no code or Zenodo artifact link; the Edinburgh open-access PDF is behind a Cloudflare challenge from this host, so I could not read the first-page footnote and cannot rule out a link there. Listed as repo unknown per the code-check rule rather than out-no-code.

title: LEANN: A Low-Storage Overhead Vector Index
note: Storage-efficient vector index that recomputes embeddings on the fly instead of storing them, explicitly targeted at personal devices and single machines. Released code, clear storage/latency/recall trade-off to push on

title: ACROBAT: Optimizing Auto-batching of Dynamic Deep Learning at Compile Time
note: Compiler + runtime for auto-batching dynamic DNNs; paper's own evaluation is a single RTX 3070, so the machine is a superset. Concern - no code URL in the paper; the repo is the first author's undocumented TVM fork (last push 2022), so a from-source TVM/CUDA build is a real risk, and baselines DyNet/Cavs must also be built.

title: λ-Tune: Harnessing Large Language Models for Automated Database System Tuning
note: LLM-driven DBMS knob tuning on PostgreSQL/MySQL; concern - needs external LLM API access

title: TOD: GPU-accelerated Outlier Detection via Tensor Operations
note: GPU outlier detection with provable memory-aware batching; explicitly designed for one GPU, PyTorch, fits 24 GB

title: NeutronStream: A Dynamic GNN Training Framework with Sliding Window for Graph Streams
note: dynamic GNN training framework; single machine CPU + one GPU

title: Graph Learning at Scale: Characterizing and Optimizing Pre-Propagation GNNs
note: GNN training-system characterization plus data-loading and training optimizations - artifact is user-space PyTorch/DGL and the PP-GNN design decouples propagation so a single A5000 is enough for medium graphs - concern: largest OGB graphs need tens of GB of disk and host RAM

title: SEIDEN: Revisiting Query Processing in Video Database Systems
note: Video database query processing that re-plans around expensive model inference; single GPU, part of the EVA ecosystem

title: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
note: Memory-efficient cascade training for federated adversarial training - evaluation is a single-machine FL simulation with per-device memory budgets - concern: more an algorithm/system hybrid, and edge-device memory claims are emulated rather than measured on real devices

title: Latency-Aware Caching with Delayed Hits: From Bursty Traffic to Pipeline Architectures
note: Pipeline of orthogonal cache policies with adaptive memory split, plus latency-aware handling of delayed hits - trace-driven simulation on top of the Caffeine framework, purely CPU and memory bound. Concern - Java build and large public cache traces need disk, both fine here.

title: Efficient Graph Data Access for Out-of-Memory GPU Streaming Graph Processing
note: Grapin caches hot subgraphs in GPU memory for out-of-core streaming graph processing - the paper itself evaluates on a single NVIDIA A5000, exactly our GPU

title: DynaCut: A Framework for Dynamic and Adaptive Program Customization
note: Binary-level, runtime code debloating - rewrites the image of a live process to disable unused or already-executed (e.g. initialization) code and re-enable it on demand, guided by execution-trace differential analysis. Entirely user-space, single-machine, and evaluated on ordinary server binaries such as Redis and Nginx that fit this box easily. Concerns - the process rewriter is a modified CRIU plus CRIT, and CRIU checkpoint/restore normally needs root or CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE; unprivileged operation would have to go through a user namespace (bwrap is available), so feasibility of the very first checkpoint must be confirmed before committing to this paper

title: MFTune: An Efficient Multi-fidelity Framework for Spark SQL Configuration Tuning
note: Multi-fidelity Spark SQL configuration tuning using representative query subsets as cheap proxies. Concern: Spark must run in local or pseudo-cluster mode

title: Flash-LLM: Enabling Low-Cost and Highly-Efficient Large Generative Model Inference With Unstructured Sparsity
note: unstructured-sparsity SpMM kernels for generative inference; A5000 is Ampere so FP16 tensor cores work and no FP8 is needed. Concern: paper uses A100 80GB with OPT-30B/66B, so a 7B-class scale-down is required

title: PiLLM: Resource-Efficient LLM Inference Using Workload Prediction
note: Workload prediction driving GPU and KV memory allocation for LLM serving - prediction and allocation policy can be studied on one GPU or from traces. No code found yet

title: Overcoming the Memory Wall with CXL-Enabled SSDs
note: Despite the CXL title, the artifact is MQSim_CXL - a pure user-space C++ simulator driven by real application memory traces. scope.md explicitly allows memory-tiering / far-memory work "studied in user space or by simulation", and no CXL hardware is touched. AE Available+Functional. Concerns: results are only as good as the simulator's fidelity, so an improvement paper has to argue about the model, not measured hardware; trace collection for new workloads would need a tracer that does not rely on perf.

title: FedTree: A Federated Learning System For Trees
note: Tree-based federated GBDT training system in C++ or CUDA - parties are simulated as processes on one host and the datasets are small - concern - homomorphic-encryption modes are slow and the secure-aggregation parts add build dependencies

title: Fast Approximate Similarity Join in Vector Databases
note: Similarity join operator for vector databases; CPU, single machine

title: Succinct and Fast Tiny Pointer Hash Tables
note: Succinct and latency-oriented hash tables built on tiny pointers with dynamic resizing; a self-contained data-structure and memory-footprint contribution

title: Decouple and Decompose: Scaling Resource Allocation with DeDe
note: Released as a plain Python package; the three case studies (cluster scheduling, traffic engineering, load balancing) are solved offline from traces on CPU only - precisely the "schedulers studied by simulation or traces" case in scope. Concern: baselines rely on a commercial solver (Gurobi academic license needed, user-space install); 16 cores limits the parallel-subproblem scaling claims.

title: Accelerating Large-Scale Reasoning Model Inference with Sparse Self-Speculative Decoding
note: Self-speculative decoding using a sparse-attention draft plus unified scheduling, delayed verification and dynamic KV management - all single-GPU systems mechanisms. Concern: headline numbers use 32B-class reasoning models that do not fit 24 GB in FP16, so scale-down or quantization is required

title: Validating JIT Compilers via Compilation Space Exploration (Artemis)
note: Entirely user-space runtime/compiler testing tool - requirements are only Java >= 11, Python >= 3.9 and Ruby >= 2.7, all installable under $HOME, no root, no GPU, no perf counters. Bug-finding throughput is a clean measurable metric for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - the value metric is bugs-found per unit time which is noisy over a 10-week window; long fuzzing campaigns are CPU-hungry on a shared machine; the AE artifact of record is Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8188346 and the maintained code is the GitHub repo

title: λ-trim: Optimizing Function Initialization in Serverless Applications With Cost-driven Debloating
note: Static analysis plus cost-driven debloating of Python serverless applications - pure user-space pipeline; concerns: end-to-end cost numbers need a real FaaS account and no official repo was found

title: RTScan:  Efficient Scan with Ray Tracing Cores
note: index scan offloaded to GPU ray-tracing cores; the A5000 is Ampere and has RT cores, OptiX works on driver 535

title: AUDIBLE: A Convolution-Based Resource Allocator for Oversubscribing Burstable Virtual Machines
note: Burstable-VM oversubscription allocator evaluated by trace-driven simulation over production traces; CPU-only and squarely within the machine budget.

title: Styx: Transactional Stateful Functions on Streaming Dataflows
note: Deterministic transactional runtime for stateful functions on a dataflow engine; concern - normally deployed as a multi-worker cluster, would run as processes on one host

title: IncrCP: Decomposing and Orchestrating Incremental Checkpoints for Effective Recommendation Model Training
note: Incremental checkpointing with 2-D chunking and dedup; the I/O and storage design is per-node and testable on one machine with NVMe. Concern: paper trains recommendation models on many devices, needs scale-down

title: MonoNN: Enabling a New Monolithic Optimization Space for Neural Network Inference Tasks on Modern GPU-Centric Architectures
note: Monolithic whole-graph GPU kernel optimization for inference - single-GPU compiler work on NVIDIA hardware. Concern - built on a specific TensorFlow/XLA and CUDA version so toolchain setup in conda is the main risk

title: LICO: An SIMD-Aware High-Performance Learned Inverted Index Compression Framework
note: SIMD-aware learned compression of inverted indexes with error-bounded models - compression plus learned data structure, CPU only

title: OptiQL: Robust Optimistic Locking for Memory-Optimized Indexes
note: Optimistic queue-based reader-writer lock for in-memory B+-tree/ART indexes - pure user-space multicore concurrency work; 16C/32T CPU is ample and no root is needed

title: R^3: Record-Replay-Retroaction for Database-Backed Applications
note: Record-replay-retroaction runtime for database-backed applications; Java services plus PostgreSQL/VoltDB, all runnable in user space on one host. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/DBOS-project/apiary/tree/r3-exp .

title: Regular Expression Indexing for Log Analysis
note: n-gram index and storage layout for regex queries over logs - user-space observability/log-analysis tooling that needs no root

title: Solving Max-Min Fair Resource Allocations Quickly on Large Graphs
note: Fast max-min fair allocators evaluated on WAN traffic engineering and cluster scheduling workloads (public Philly traces); Python plus C# with Gurobi, CPU only, trace-driven. Concerns: needs a Gurobi academic license and .NET installed in user space; the contribution is algorithmic, so an improvement project would be about solver formulations and approximation quality rather than systems engineering.

title: Memory Management in Complex Join Queries: A Re-evaluation Study
note: Re-evaluates 1990s memory-distribution policies across join operators using a modified AsterixDB - user-space memory budgeting, single node, JVM only (Java installable via conda). Directly matches the course's fallback "careful reproduction" track and leaves obvious room for an improved memory-distribution policy. Concerns - original runs were on AWS HDD/SSD instances, so device-level results will differ; it is a study paper, so the "improvement" angle has to be supplied by the team.

title: GriNNder: Breaking the Memory Capacity Wall in Full-Graph GNN Training with Storage Offloading
note: Full-graph GNN training on a single server by offloading to NVMe SSDs - designed exactly for the limited-GPU-memory single-node setting. Concerns: NVMe is software RAID and shared and only ~257 GB is free so the largest graphs will not fit; uses kvikio/GPUDirect-style paths that may fall back to buffered I/O without privileges

title: Arctic: A Practical Lock-Free Adaptive Radix Tree
note: Ideal fit: a lock-free index benchmarked with YCSB and integrated into RocksDB and Turso, all user space, and 16 cores / 32 threads is enough to show scaling. Concern: Rust must be installed in user space (fine via rustup/conda); some scalability claims target higher core counts

title: PartIR: Composing SPMD Partitioning Strategies for Machine Learning
note: PartIR SPMD partitioning IR with a predictable rewrite API and a simulator; concern: targets multi-device training and no public repo found by GitHub/web search

title: SkipKV: Selective Skipping of KV Generation and Storage for Efficient Inference with Large Reasoning Models
note: Training-free sentence-level KV eviction plus steering-vector generation control for reasoning models; single GPU, released code. Concern: the strongest results use large reasoning models, so 7-8B or quantized variants are needed to stay within 24 GB

title: Sesame: Practical End-to-End Privacy Compliance with Policy Containers and Privacy Regions
note: Rust framework (actively maintained) enforcing privacy policies inside web applications; user space, no root, evaluated as request-latency/throughput overhead against unmodified baselines - a directly measurable performance axis on this machine. Concern: compliance/privacy framing rather than an OS resource-management topic; the evaluation apps need a local database and web stack stood up by hand.

title: TreeCat: Standalone Catalog Engine for Large Data Systems
note: Standalone catalog storage engine with a versioned range-optimized format and concurrent readers and writers; single node with code released

title: On Efficient Approximate Queries over Machine Learning Models
note: Approximate query processing that minimises expensive ML model invocations using cheap proxy models; one GPU is enough

title: PRISM: A Training System to Unlock the Potential of Temporal Graph Learning Through Staleness Avoidance
note: Multi-versioned memory training system for temporal GNNs that removes staleness without losing GPU parallelism; single-GPU training system

title: SWIFT: Enabling Large-Scale Temporal Graph Learning on a Single Machine
note: temporal graph learning system explicitly designed for a single machine - GPU training system that fits the box - concern: no abstract or repo located

title: Why Database Manuals Are Not Enough: Efficient and Reliable Configuration Tuning for DBMSs via Code-Driven LLM Agents
note: Mines knob tuning rules from DBMS source code with static analysis plus LLM reasoning; the tuning loop runs against a local PostgreSQL or MySQL

title: CoMPI: Coordinated Model Merging and Parallel Inference at Edge
note: Jointly optimizes model merging (parameter sharing to cut GPU memory) and parallel deployment for multi-model edge inference under memory pressure - the memory-pressure regime maps well onto one 24 GB GPU. Repo description matches the paper and was last pushed 2025-11-21, the SoCC presentation date. Concerns - repository authorship was inferred from the description and timing rather than from a link in the paper; the paper assumes a small multi-GPU edge cluster, so a single-GPU scale-down is needed.

title: NeuStream: Bridging Deep Learning Serving and Stream Processing
note: Module-granularity batching and two-level scheduling for serving DNNs with control flow, including LLMs and diffusion models; diffusion pipelines and 7B LLMs fit one 24 GB GPU. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper's larger multi-GPU serving configurations must be scaled down to one GPU

title: EarthSight: A Distributed Framework for Low-Latency Satellite Intelligence
note: Ground-station query scheduler plus dynamic filter ordering, evaluated with a Python constellation simulator, so the scheduling contribution is trace/simulation driven and fits one machine. Concerns: the paper says EarthSight is open-sourced but no repository URL appears in the PDF, hyperlinks or GitHub search, so the repo is unknown

title: CUBIT: Concurrent Updatable Bitmap Indexing
note: Latch-free concurrent updatable bitmap index - pure user-space C++ structure whose claim is scaling with core count; 16 cores / 32 threads is enough to reproduce the trend

title: Simple Adaptive Query Processing vs. Learned Query Optimizers: Observations and Analysis
note: Head-to-head study of adaptive query processing versus learned query optimizers; already a reproduction-style paper, easy hypothesis to extend on PostgreSQL

title: ParaSync: Exploiting Fine-Grained Parallelism for Efficient File Synchronization
note: Parallel content-defined chunking + streaming chunk matching + pipelined reconstruction; user-space C++, CPU-bound, benefits from the 16-core/32-thread CPU. Same WAN-emulation caveat as SkySync; chunking speedup (7.6x claimed) is measurable locally with no privileges.

title: COLE: A Column-based Learned Storage for Blockchain Systems
note: Learned-index-based column storage replacing Ethereum's Merkle Patricia Trie, with write-optimized (LSM-like) strategies for disk. Rust, single machine, ordinary NVMe - exactly this hardware class. Clean improvement axes (model choice, merge policy, provenance query cost). No GPU, no root, no cluster.

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference via Global Analysis and Tensor Expressions
note: Inter-operator DNN inference compiler; single NVIDIA GPU evaluation. Concern - artifact is packaged with Docker files that must be reproduced with conda/pip since Docker is unavailable.

title: Scalable and Robust Snapshot Isolation for High-Performance Storage Engines
note: MVCC/snapshot-isolation redesign inside the LeanStore storage engine; single-node NVMe C++, benchmarks via BenchBase. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/mvcc .

title: Turbocharging Vector Databases using Modern SSDs
note: SSD-aware pgvector optimizations using io_uring parallel I/O, insertion reordering and locality-preserving colocation; io_uring needs no root

title: Validating Large Language Models with ReLM
note: System that compiles regular expressions into constrained decoding over an LLM - single-GPU inference on GPT-2 or GPT-J class models and a direct ancestor of todays structured-generation stacks - concern - the largest models in the paper need quantization to fit 24 GB

title: Rose: Reproducing External-Fault-Induced Failures in Distributed Systems with Lightweight Instrumentation
note: Lightweight user-space tracing plus fault schedule generation to reproduce external-fault failures - the instrumentation and replay can run against systems started as local processes, artifact available. Concern: targets distributed systems

title: Scalable GPU Acceleration of Scalar Functions in Analytical Databases: Compilation, Benchmarking and Optimization
note: LLVM MLIR toolchain that lifts production CPU scalar function implementations into GPU kernels plus a benchmark that stresses scalar functions; single-GPU compiler work

title: Zombie Hashing: Reanimating Tombstones in Graveyard
note: Linear-probing hash table redesign to avoid rebuild stalls; user-space data structure

title: A Resource-centric Analysis and Optimization of NoSQL Workloads using Distressed Resource Volume Metric
note: Open-sourced Cosmos DB replica traces plus the LoadStar policy simulator for packing and migration; trace-driven resource-management study with no cluster needed. Concern: artifact is behind an aka.ms redirect

title: High-performance Effective Scientific Error-bounded Lossy Compression with Auto-tuned Multi-component Interpolation
note: Error-bounded lossy compressor with auto-tuned interpolation; CPU only, user-space build

title: ValScope: Value-Semantics-Aware Metamorphic Testing for Detecting Logical Bugs in DBMSs
note: User-space DBMS test-oracle generator (SQL query approximation + metamorphic relations); runs entirely against local SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL builds with no root. Concern: the "improvement" metric is bugs found, which is noisy over a 10-week window - a performance/coverage angle would be safer

title: TriInfer: Hybrid EPD Disaggregation for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Model Inference
note: Encode-prefill-decode disaggregation for multimodal LLM serving with stage-level batching, released code and vLLM/SGLang baselines. Concern: the three stages are meant to run on separate heterogeneous instances, so a single-GPU study means co-locating stages or using MPS

title: Arbitor: A Numerically Accurate Hardware Emulation Tool for DNN Accelerators
note: An ML-compiler-based emulator that runs on general-purpose GPUs - it deliberately avoids needing accelerator hardware, and the topic (ML compiler / runtime tooling) is in scope. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the sensitivity study trains ResNet/Transformer/RNN/GNN models; on one 24 GB A5000 only scaled-down models and shortened schedules are feasible, and emulated low-precision arithmetic is slow.

title: FastTree: Optimizing Attention Kernel and Runtime for Tree-Structured LLM Inference
note: Radix-tree-aware attention kernels and runtime on top of SGLang - artifact states the Triton kernels use no Hopper-specific features, so an Ampere GPU works with reduced absolute numbers

title: Practical Verification of System-Software Components Written in Standard C
note: TPot is a user-space SMT-based verifier for C system software; CPU-only, no root, and verification wall-clock time is a clean quantitative target for an improvement hypothesis. Concern: proof engineering rather than resource management; topic fit rests on the other-userspace catch-all.

title: Cheddar: A Swift Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library Designed for GPU Architectures
note: CUDA CKKS library; pure user-space GPU code that fits a single A5000

title: LeanAttention: Hardware-Aware Scalable Attention Mechanism for the Decode-Phase of Transformers
note: Exact decode-phase attention kernel (stream-K style splitting) - pure CUDA kernel work on one GPU - concerns: no standalone repo, the official implementation is the LeanAttention kernel merged into ONNX Runtime contrib_ops/cuda/bert, and paper numbers are on A100/H100 so absolute speedups on Ampere A5000 will differ

title: Elf: Erasing-based Lossless Floating-Point Compression
note: Erasing-based lossless floating-point compression for time-series storage; Java, single node, modest datasets
